record.original_question: Fix a class C of matrices and let C_n denote the subclass of matrices in C of order at most n. Let l(A) be the smallest real eigenvalue of A, and consider the spectral angle bound |arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π/2 − π/n for every eigenvalue λ in σ(A). What is the largest integer n for which every matrix in C_n satisfies this inequality? The paper asks this for the same four classes: A_{n,k,t}, GKK τ-matrices, GKK matrices, and τ-matrices.

evidence.quote: showed that τ -matrices of order up to 4 satisfy the inequality |arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π / 2 − π / n ∀λ ∈ σ(A), (2)
3b. What is the maximum n such that all matrices in class Cn satisfy (2)?

Speciﬁc classes C of interest include i. The class of matrices An,k,t for positive integers n and k, and for t ∈ (0, 1), ii. The class of GKK τ -matrices, iii. The class of GKK matrices, iv. The class of τ -matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

For a square complex matrix $A$, let $\sigma(A)$ denote its spectrum. Assume throughout that $A$ has at least one real eigenvalue, and write $l(A)$ for the smallest real eigenvalue of $A$. For a nonzero complex number $z$, let $\arg(z) \in (-\pi,\pi]$ denote its principal argument.

A matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is called a $\tau$-matrix if every principal submatrix $B$ of $A$ (including $A$ itself) has a real eigenvalue and its smallest real eigenvalue $l(B)$ satisfies $l(B) \le l(C)$ for every principal submatrix $C$ of $B$ (i.e., the smallest real eigenvalue is monotone non-decreasing under taking principal submatrices). A matrix $A$ is called a GKK matrix if all principal minors of $A$ are positive and $A$ is weakly sign-symmetric, meaning $a_{ij} a_{ji} \ge 0$ for all $i,j$. A GKK $\tau$-matrix is a matrix that is simultaneously a GKK matrix and a $\tau$-matrix.

For positive integers $n,k$ and $t \in (0,1)$, let $A_{n,k,t}$ denote the matrix class consisting of $n \times n$ matrices defined by certain $k$- and $t$-parametrized constructions arising in the study of the above classes (the same family $A_{n,k,t}$ used to study stability of GKK and $\tau$-matrices).

The spectral angle inequality. For an $n \times n$ matrix $A$ with $l(A)$ defined, consider the inequality
$$|\arg(\lambda - l(A))| \le \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{n}, \qquad \text{for every } \lambda \in \sigma(A). \tag{$\ast$}$$

Problem. For each of the following four classes $\mathcal{C}$ of matrices, let $\mathcal{C}_n$ denote the subclass consisting of those members of $\mathcal{C}$ whose order is at most $n$. Determine the largest integer $n$ such that every matrix $A \in \mathcal{C}_n$ satisfies $(\ast)$:

(i) $\mathcal{C} = \{A_{n,k,t} : n,k \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0},\ t \in (0,1)\}$;
(ii) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of GKK $\tau$-matrices;
(iii) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of GKK matrices;
(iv) $\mathcal{C}$ = the class of $\tau$-matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces the original list of open problems on GKK τ-matrices and a later counterexample paper showing not all GKK τ-matrices are stable, but no source resolving the specific threshold question on the spectral angle inequality |arg(λ−l(A))| ≤ π/2 − π/n for the four named classes was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples constructed showing instability, but the spectral angle threshold problem is not resolved.
